- When sentiment is negative or neutral in recent days, model tends to underpredict sharp upward moves; adjust forecast upward by 1–3% for early spikes.
- After a strong downward spike in history, model often fails to rebound quickly; add 2–5% upward bias in next 5–7 days if sentiment turns positive.
- If model shows steady downward trend with no recent sentiment shift, it underestimates mean reversion; add 1–3% upward bias in 3–5 day horizon.
- When sentiment is positive and price is falling, model often overcorrects downward; add 1–2% upward bias to prevent overshoot.
- If true outcome shows large divergence from forecast in first 5–7 days (e.g., >5% drop or rise), model is lagging; adjust forecast to match recent 3–5 day true trend.
- For 30-day horizon, model consistently underestimates upward momentum after sentiment turns positive; add 2–4% upward bias if sentiment >0.5 in last 5 days.
- If sentiment is negative and model forecast is flat or declining, it underestimates volatility; add 1–3% upward bias to account for potential reversal.
